(Retrieved via WebFetch; condensed by fetch tool)

The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding on June 17, extending their ceasefire by 60 days. The agreement included provisions to continue detailed negotiations on the Strait of Hormuz's future, Iran's frozen assets, long-term sanctions relief, and Tehran's nuclear programme.

Talks location: Doha, Qatar.

Negotiators:
- US side: Steve Witkoff (US envoy) and Jared Kushner (US President Donald Trump's son-in-law)
- Iranian side: technical delegations; Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Consultative Assembly Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf notably reluctant to attend in person
- Mediator: Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani

Quotes:
US Vice President JD Vance stated the administration was in a "great position" regardless of outcome and that Iran would be "permanently transformed" if negotiations succeed.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran expected "$6bn of the frozen Iranian funds to be released by the US as a first step."
